content.text:
My take: good direction, but I’d request changes before merging. The PR fixes real problems, yet introduces several security and isolation regressions.

- **Blocker — credentialed CORS becomes allow-any-origin.** With `origin: '*'` and `credentials: true`, the middleware reflects every caller’s origin. Previously the invalid wildcard combination was browser-blocked; now a malicious site can read credentialed responses. Require an allowlist/predicate or reject this configuration. [Code/thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/109#discussion_r3551412934), [CORS guidance](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Practical_implementation_guides/CORS).

- **Blocker — SQLite transactions are not isolated.** Explicit `BEGIN` around an awaited callback leaves the shared connection inside that transaction while the callback is suspended. Other requests can execute inside it. I reproduced this locally: an “outside” insert was silently removed by the transaction’s rollback. The connection needs serialization/mutexing around transactions and ordinary queries. [Code/thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/109#discussion_r3551412918).

- **High — `maxBodyBytes` is bypassable for multipart bodies.** `formData()` checks only `Content-Length`; chunked requests without that header are parsed without any limit. The streamed reader should also be cancelled when the limit is exceeded. [Code/thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/109#discussion_r3551412926).

- **High — GitHub revocation Basic auth is encoded incorrectly.** The implementation percent-encodes the client ID/secret before Base64, while GitHub expects them directly as the Basic username/password. The test uses characters for which encoding is a no-op, so it misses this. [Code/thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/109#discussion_r3551784619), [GitHub endpoint documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/apps/oauth-applications?apiVersion=2022-11-28).

- **High if webhook URLs are untrusted — the SSRF protection is incomplete.** Restricting schemes still permits `http://127.0.0.1`, cloud metadata addresses, private networks, DNS rebinding, and redirects to those targets. It needs a destination policy that validates resolved IPs and every redirect hop, or the change should stop claiming SSRF protection. [Code/thread](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/pull/109#discussion_r3551412939).

- **Smaller regression — 405 responses bypass `onError`.** The new branch returns directly, whereas the previous 404 path went through the configured error handler. Applications using custom error envelopes or observability will get inconsistent behavior. [Router code](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/24313a460563fa149dd540a77625ae007c60c9d4/packages/http/src/router.ts#L99).

The positive pieces—fail-closed resource auth, redirect allowlisting, `Vary: Origin`, empty-`where` protection, queue limits, and explicit WHERE grouping—are worthwhile. However, the “each fix has test coverage” claim is overstated: no changed tests directly cover the Prisma/Kysely/memory safeguards, storage backpressure, signed-URL expiry, metrics errors, or OAuth timeout/expiry behavior.

The PR remains a draft with five unresolved threads. Its CI jobs did not actually run because the GitHub account was locked for billing, so the failure is infrastructural rather than evidence of broken code—but the local test-count claims remain externally unverified. [CI run](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/actions/runs/29019903372).

I’d fix the five substantive findings, add focused regression tests, then rerun CI before considering it merge-ready.
